To implement supervised training of AST on SAM, we modify the methodology described in Mehri and Eskenazi (2021), which embeds both conversation and schema elements to produce an attention vector $p$ . Here, $p_i$ gives the attention weight between the conversation and the $i$ -th user action of the policy graph. This is then interpreted to be a proxy for probability, and converted to a probability for NAP on all system actions $a$ according to the policy

graph edges:

$$
\begin{array}{l} g (i, a) = \left\{ \begin{array}{l l} p _ {i}, & \text {i f a c t i o n (n e x t} (u _ {i})) = a \\ 0, & \text {o t h e r w i s e} \end{array} \right. \\ P (a) = \sum_ {i \leq | S |} g (i, a) \\ \end{array}
$$

Here, action $(\mathrm{next}(u_i))$ gives the next system action of the user action $u_{i}$ according to the policy graph. Note that $p_i$ is an attention weight that is intercepted to be the probability of user action $u_{i}$ being active at the current turn; however, no supervised training was done with ground truth user action labels. Then, to implement supervised training on these user actions, we train $p_i$ to be actual probabilities, and apply a sigmoid on $p_i$ to form a user action prediction head. Note that this is a

multilabel binary prediction. We then calculate a binary cross-entropy loss on this head.
